source.title: Rethinking the limiting dynamics of SGD: modified loss, phase space oscillations, and anomalous diffusion
source.authors: D. Kunin; Javier Sagastuy-Breña; Lauren Gillespie; Eshed Margalit; Hidenori Tanaka; S. Ganguli; Daniel Yamins

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no relevant truncation or garbling beyond apparent PDF extraction artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures how optimization hyperparameters relate to parameter displacement and diffusion in pretrained networks, including a ResNet-18 ImageNet sweep. These findings concern training dynamics rather than the listed generalization-gap versions, so they are recorded as findings that fit no version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports resumed-training results on displacement, loss contours, and phase-space trajectories. It does not measure random-label memorization, held-out error gaps across the listed conditions, or magnitude-aware sharpness. Those results do not establish any listed version; cited results from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests predictions about SGD parameter and velocity dynamics, not any of V1–V8. Its batch-size sweep measures displacement and diffusion, not held-out performance; its Hessian projections do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or its association with generalization gaps. References to generalization findings are background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive a conditional theory involving a modified loss, velocity regularization, and phase-space probability currents, and report qualitative and quantitative evidence for its predictions in resumed ImageNet training. They do not establish an effect on generalization performance.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies resumed training of pretrained networks and a linear-regression setting, measuring parameter and velocity dynamics rather than generalization error, memorization, or the listed interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: For the ResNet-18 sweep, learning rate, batch size, and momentum each affect the fitted diffusion exponent; larger learning rate lowers the exponent, while batch size has a non-monotonic influence. The exponent also increases with fitted trajectory length in Appendix I.7.

fits_no_version.finding: Five pretrained ImageNet classifiers retain approximately constant local displacement while global squared displacement grows with fitted exponents 1.075–1.616; the ResNet-18 exponent also depends on trajectory length.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Resumed SGD training of pretrained image classifiers exhibits persistent parameter movement and anomalous diffusion over the measured trajectories.

fits_no_version.finding: Predicted mean position and velocity trajectories nearly match measured linear-regression trajectories on CIFAR-10 under the tested momentum settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The derived oscillator model approximates the tested linear-regression training trajectories.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet-18 trajectories show qualitative parameter-space isotropy, inverse-Hessian-shaped velocity contours, and different oscillation rates in two Hessian projections.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selected projections of pretrained ResNet-18's limiting dynamics exhibit the modified-loss and oscillation patterns predicted by the theory.

fits_no_version.finding: Learning rate, batch size, and momentum alter local displacement and the fitted diffusion exponent during resumed ResNet-18 training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimization hyperparameters influence parameter transport in the limiting dynamics of a pretrained ResNet-18.

record.problems: The paper's neural-network empirical evidence is largely qualitative in plotted projections and fitted trajectories. It assumes a Gaussian gradient-noise model and an approximately quadratic loss near the end of training; the authors state the latter is strong and note that negative Hessian eigenvalues are inconsistent with the positive-semidefinite assumption. The ImageNet Hessian estimate uses a subset of 40,000 training images.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible result rows were left out.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed to fit training data.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance under different tuning recipes.
Large- versus small-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout's effects on held-out error across training-set sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T3 classification conflicts with its correctly unlinked rows. The dynamics findings can be observed in their own terms, but their states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8. No listed-version results are missing.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label test accuracy comparison.
No width sweep or test-error measurement beyond interpolation.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No large versus small batch held-out performance comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measure or comparison of generalization gaps.

rows.subject: Linear Regression
rows.operation_detail: Compared projected position and velocity trajectories with a theoretically derived mean under different momentum settings.
rows.measure: Agreement of projected position and velocity trajectories with equation (9)
rows.value: The theoretically derived mean nearly perfectly matches empirics under various hyperparameter settings.
rows.note: The text reports the comparison in aggregate across the two momentum settings.
rows.check: Agreement between predicted and measured linear-regression trajectories does not measure any listed generalization effect.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained on ImageNet; training resumed for 5 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Projected the parameter trajectory onto Hessian eigenvectors and compared its path with sampled training, test, and modified-loss contours.
rows.measure: Qualitative isotropy of projected trajectory despite anisotropic training and test loss contours
rows.value: The trajectory appears to cover both directions equally; it is described as isotropic despite the anisotropy of the training and test loss.
rows.note: The authors call this qualitative evidence for dynamics in a modified isotropic loss landscape.
rows.check: Isotropy of a projected trajectory relative to loss contours does not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or rank generalization gaps.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained on ImageNet; training resumed for 5 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Projected the velocity trajectory onto Hessian eigenvectors and compared its shape with inverse-Hessian modified-loss contours.
rows.measure: Similarity between projected velocity trajectory and inverse-Hessian contours
rows.value: The shape of the projected velocity trajectory closely resembles the contours of the modified loss Ψv.
rows.check: Velocity regularization is a dynamics finding, with no measurement of any listed generalization effect.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained on ImageNet; training resumed for 5 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Examined projected position and velocity paths in phase space for two Hessian eigenvectors.
rows.measure: Phase-space trajectory pattern and oscillation rates
rows.value: Both trajectories look like noisy clockwise rotations; oscillations at different rates are distinguishable for the different eigenvectors.
rows.note: The paper also states the frequency difference was verified by comparing dominant FFT frequencies.
rows.check: Phase-space oscillations and their frequencies do not measure any listed generalization effect.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained on ImageNet; training resumed for 2 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Swept learning rate, batch size, and momentum separately and measured local displacement and fitted global-displacement exponent.

conditions.value: 20 evenly spaced values for one hyperparameter at a time
All except the swept hyperparameter held at default

rows.measure: Squared local displacement ∥δt∥² and fitted global-displacement exponent c
rows.baseline: Default hyperparameter setting shown in black; predicted instantaneous-speed line from equation (18)
rows.value: Learning rate, batch size, and momentum can each independently drive c into different regimes; larger learning rate reduces c, and batch size has a non-monotonic influence on c. The measured local displacement is reported to match equation (18).
rows.note: The paper does not give numeric sweep values in the supplied text; Figure 7 displays the sweep. It reports the trends and an exact match to the predicted local-displacement relation.
rows.check: Displacement and diffusion under batch-size changes cannot test V5 without held-out performance comparisons. Correct the note claiming numeric sweep values are unavailable: Table 4 gives 20 evenly spaced values spanning batch sizes 32–1024, learning rates 10^-3–10^-5, and momentum 0.8–0.99.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained on ImageNet; resumed training trajectory lengths vary from 20 to 100 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Refit a power law to global-displacement trajectories as the fitted trajectory length increased.
rows.measure: Fitted exponent c for squared global displacement ∥∆k∥² ∝ kᶜ
rows.value: The fitted exponent c increases at a diminishing rate with the length of the trajectory; reported values range from c = 1.069 at 20 epochs to c = 1.306 at 100 epochs.
rows.note: Figure text reports each trajectory length and exponent; the paper describes the increase and possible sum-of-power-laws interpretation.
rows.check: Dependence of a fitted diffusion exponent on trajectory length does not measure any listed generalization effect.
